title: drymocallis ashlandica
intro: Drymocallis ashlandica, commonly known as Ashland sticky geranium, is a plant species in the rose family that is native to the mountainous regions of the Pacific Northwest. It has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which may help to soothe skin irritations, reduce fever, and protect against cell damage. The therapeutic actions of Ashland sticky geranium include its ability to act as an antiseptic, astringent, and vulnerary, making it useful for wound healing and skin conditions. The bioactive constituents of Drymocallis ashlandica include iridoids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
